description: Conformance corpus for standards/http.md. 'validity': the value must validate (or fail) against the named $def — 'problem' for problem.schema.json's root, or a $def name in pagination.schema.json. 'behaviour': black-box cases a live service must satisfy; the harness drives the stimulus and asserts 'expect'. An implementation passes the whole file or names the case it fails.

value.title: Subscription not found
value.detail: no subscription with public id sub_8fK2mQ7xW3pLzR exists for this tenant

validity.note: detail names the specific thing looked for, by public id rather than internal key (HA3, IP1)

errors.message: starts_at must be RFC 3339 UTC with three fractional digits

validity.note: a client highlighting two bad inputs can do it from errors[]; it could not from detail alone (HA3)
about:blank is admitted where the status code is the whole story — an unrouted path is exactly that case (HA3)

value.title: Subscription not found
value.detail: no subscription with public id sub_8fK2mQ7xW3pLzR exists for this tenant

validity.note: request_id is what turns a screenshot of an error into a log query; without it the envelope is a dead end (HA3, OC2)
title names the class and detail carries this occurrence's reason; a class without a reason is the SC2 failure on a different surface (HA3)
rule is the stable slug a client branches on; without it the client is parsing prose (HA3)
filtering can empty a page; empty does not mean the end, which is exactly why next_cursor and not data length is the signal (HA4)
an absent next_cursor makes the end of a list a guess (HA4)

behaviour.stimulus: GET a path no route matches
behaviour.note: the most common failure in the portfolio today: a framework's default HTML error page escaping to clients from the one path nobody wrote a handler for (HA3)

behaviour.stimulus: POST a body with two fields violating the OpenAPI schema

expect.body.errors: one entry per rejected field, each with field, rule and message

behaviour.stimulus: POST a mutating endpoint twice with the same Idempotency-Key and identical body

expect.second_response: byte-identical status and body to the first

behaviour.note: this is what makes HA7's retries safe by contract rather than by luck (HA6)

behaviour.stimulus: POST twice with the same Idempotency-Key and a changed body
behaviour.note: silently serving the first response to a second, different request is worse than refusing (HA6)
a 429 without Retry-After tells a client to back off by an amount it must guess, and every client guesses differently and wrongly (HA7)

behaviour.stimulus: page through a collection using only the returned next_cursor
behaviour.note: the property offset pagination cannot hold over a changing collection (HA4)
